summary: Backend-only test of the new refusal-cause-code analytics instrumentation (A4). Verified /api/chat/stream refusal + success paths, db.refusal_events privacy-safe schema, GET /api/admin/refusal-stats shape/auth, and regression of /api/admin/stats + CSV exports. Feature itself works correctly. However, discovered a PRE-EXISTING CRITICAL retrieval false-positive bug (not part of this session's changes, but it directly breaks the exact test scenarios given in the review request) — see critical_code_review_comments.

critical.issue: The two example refusal queries given in the review request ('What is the punishment for cheque bounce under section 138?' and 'How do I get a divorce under Hindu Marriage Act?') do NOT refuse. Instead corpus.retrieve() returns unrelated corpus entries as false-positive matches (e.g. cheque-bounce/'138' query matches 'Central Motor Vehicles Rules, Rule 138(3) — seat belts' purely because of the numeral '138'; the divorce query matches 'IPC Section 294 — obscene acts'). The LLM then answers with hallucinated, non-corpus-backed legal specifics (e.g. invented cheque-bounce penalty details, invented divorce procedure) while displaying an unrelated citation chip. This violates the app's own citation-integrity rule and is a safety issue for a legal-aid product, and it also means the refusal_events cause_code breakdown will under-count true corpus gaps because many out-of-scope queries silently get a wrong answer + fabricated citation instead of registering as a refusal.

action_items: Fix corpus.py scoring (_score_all/_token_weight) so a bare numeral like '138' or a single generic word cannot alone push an unrelated entry past RETRIEVAL_MIN_SCORE=3 — require the numeral to co-occur with a matching Act prefix, or raise the weight/threshold for numeral-only matches.

Consider extending the existing citation-integrity void-check (server.py ~line 563-582) to also void retrieval when the query contains a bare section number with NO Act prefix and the retrieved short_label's number doesn't match — currently only covers queries that DO include an Act prefix (BNS/BNSS/IPC/etc).
Re-run this analytics test suite after the retrieval fix — with the false positives gone, more real queries will correctly hit the refusal path and refusal_events will fill in as intended.
No changes needed to refusal_events/admin-refusal-stats code itself — it is correct and privacy-safe as implemented.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py chat_stream(): refusal_events insertion (lines ~588-634) correctly stores ONLY id, cause_code, sub_cause, category, language, state(null), top_score, top_key, created_at — no user_id/session_id/raw query text. Verified via direct MongoDB inspection.

corpus.py top_candidate_debug()/classify_topic()/_score_all() refactor: retrieve() cutoff (RETRIEVAL_MIN_SCORE=3) behavior is unchanged as claimed — confirmed via passing regression tests on known-good/known-refused queries.

GET /api/admin/refusal-stats correctly reuses _check_admin_key() (same HMAC-safe compare as /api/admin/stats and /api/admin/export/*), rejects missing/wrong key with 401, and its by_cause_code counts sum to total_refusals.

Design note (not a bug): cause_code for corpus-gap refusals is always 'no_corpus_match', with the finer 'no_candidate_scored' / 'below_confidence_threshold' / 'query_too_vague' distinction living in sub_cause instead of cause_code. This matches the endpoint's own by_sub_cause breakdown and is a reasonable design, just flagging in case the product owner expected those to be top-level cause codes as the problem statement's phrasing implied.

success_rate.frontend: not tested this round (backend-only per request); light smoke of chat/stream SSE confirmed no console/stream errors

seed_data_creation: None (test-only refusal_events docs created via real chat calls; not cleaned up as collection is analytics/aggregate-only, no PII).
context_for_next_testing_agent: IMPORTANT: run backend/tests/test_refusal_analytics.py with `pytest tests/test_refusal_analytics.py -n 0` (serial) — under the default `-n 2 --dist loadscope` from pytest.ini, count-based assertions on db.refusal_events race across parallel test classes and produce false failures (verified: same 2 tests fail every parallel run, pass every serial run). This is a test-isolation artifact, not an app bug. The bare-numeral retrieval false-positive (cheque-bounce '138' -> CMVR seat-belt '138(3)') is the one real bug found — it predates this session's changes but was newly exposed by trying the review request's own example queries.
rca_of_issue: Root cause of retrieval false positives: corpus.py's _score_all() gives +1 'weak signal' weight per common token overlap plus scores numerals like '138' as ordinary tokens; when a query contains a bare number that happens to match an unrelated corpus entry's rule/section number (e.g. 'section 138' vs 'CMVR Rule 138(3)'), or several generic words (e.g. 'medical', 'hospital', 'person') that overlap with an unrelated entry's keyword list, the accumulated score can reach RETRIEVAL_MIN_SCORE=3 even though the entry is semantically unrelated. The existing identifier-voiding safety check in server.py only fires when the query explicitly names an Act prefix (BNS/BNSS/BSA/IPC/CrPC/PWDVA/RTI/CPA/MV/MVA) alongside the number — a bare 'section 138' with no prefix bypasses it entirely.
